patch.value: GH-1643: pm claim --next --start is refused with 'Specify an item id or pass --next' although --next was passed; select-claim-start needs one atomic write

https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1643

Reproduced on the current source build (2026.10.31) in a fresh non-git sandbox: `pm claim --next --start` exits 2 with the generic command_failed refusal 'Specify an item id or pass --next' and refusal.surface --next. Root cause: runClaimAction in src/cli/register-operations.ts routes any --start to requireClaimTarget(id, false), which ignores --next and emits the hint to pass the flag already passed. The MCP transport has the same defect: runMcpClaimAction (src/sdk/lifecycle/mcp-actions.ts) routes start to runMcpTaskCompositionAction, which requires an explicit id and refuses with 'Missing required argument: id'.

Selecting, claiming and starting the next item is one agent intent. Today it takes claim --next followed by update --status in_progress: a crash between the two leaves a claimed-but-open item. claim --next already selects and claims under the item lock with an advancing race-loss walk (pm-114v, pm-fjxm). release --handoff already changes status inside the release mutation with enforceTypeWorkflowTransition (src/sdk/lifecycle/release-handoff.ts), so the same pattern gives an atomic claim-and-start.

Duplicate search: 'claim next start', 'refusal suggests flag already provided', GH-1352, GH-1643; nearest are pm-114v and pm-fjxm (claim --next, closed), pm-gh1369 (claim --start compact receipts, closed), pm-ixi1 (provided flag listed as missing, closed) and pm-f05lsg (refusal closure gate, open).

pm claim --next --start selects, claims and moves the selected item to the workspace's in-progress status in one locked mutation with one history event, honours the selection filters, --if-available and the race-loss walk, enforces configured type workflows, and reports the start transition in the receipt; MCP pm_claim with next and start behaves identically; a claim target refusal never tells the caller to pass a flag already present and carries a typed code; regression tests cover CLI, MCP and the refusal hint
pm claim --next --start atomically claims and starts the next available item on CLI, MCP and SDK, and no claim-target refusal recommends a flag the caller already supplied.

value.text: Implementation: runClaim gained an optional start that calls applyClaimStart inside the same mutateItem callback (the release --handoff pattern). It resolves the in-progress status through resolveStartTaskInProgressStatus, refuses a terminal item with terminal_state_conflict even under --force, enforces type workflows via enforceTypeWorkflowTransition, and returns start {from_status,to_status}. runClaimNext forwards start to every candidate in the race-loss walk, so --if-available and filters behave as before. CLI runClaimAction and MCP runMcpClaimAction route start with an explicit id to the unchanged two-step composition, which keeps its typed 'Remove --next and --if-available' refusal; start without an id uses the atomic path or the new requireClaimTarget in src/sdk/lifecycle/claim-target.ts (missing_required_argument / ambiguous_option_combination, attributed to claim through the catalog generator's module map). runStartTask now strips start before its claim step so explicit --start stays claim-then-update. MCP schema: the start+next exclusion is gone and start+ifAvailable is exclusive only with an id. PmClient.claimNext({start:true}) is typed. Verified in a sandbox: claim --next --start → status in_progress, changed_field_count 3, history create→claim (one event).

patch.value: pm claim --next --start claims and starts the next available item in one write on every transport, and no claim-target refusal recommends a flag the caller supplied.

runClaim accepts start and applyClaimStart moves the claimed item to the configured in-progress status inside the same mutateItem callback. That gives one claim history event, type-workflow enforcement, terminal_state_conflict for terminal items, and a start {from_status,to_status} receipt. runClaimNext forwards start through the race-loss walk. The CLI runClaimAction and MCP runMcpClaimAction route an id-less start to that path, while an explicit-id start keeps the claim-then-update composition and its typed refusal. requireClaimTarget now lives in the SDK claim module with missing_required_argument and ambiguous_option_combination codes and never names a flag the caller already passed. PmClient.claimNext accepts start. The MCP schema drops the start+next exclusion, and start+ifAvailable is exclusive only with an id.

Sandbox: pm claim --next --start returns status in_progress with changed_field_count 3 and history create then claim. MCP claim {next,start} and PmClient.claimNext({start:true}) return in_progress. pm claim --start refuses with missing_required_argument, suggesting pm claim --next --start. claim-start spec 7/7, register-commands 91/91, and lifecycle integration specs pass. With the routing stashed, the CLI/MCP start test fails. Full suite 11,748 passed.
Fixed: claim --next --start is one locked select-claim-start write on CLI, MCP and SDK

value.text: CodeRabbit review round 1 on PR #1645. (1) The compact claim receipt now keeps the start {from_status,to_status} object (mutation-projection copies plain-object start), so default CLI JSON and MCP responses show the transition. (2) Major, predates this PR: resolveStartTaskInProgressStatus ignored a configured in_progress_status. A workflow declaring in_progress_status 'working' started items into the open status. It now returns the registry's in-progress status when it differs from the open status, and otherwise keeps the in_progress alias lookup (the 'building' alias workflow still resolves). Registration tests cover both. (3) Semantic attribution after the claim commit is best-effort: a failure returns the warning claim_semantic_attribution_unrecorded instead of an error for persisted ownership (claim-attribution spec). (4) MCP claim {id, next, start} was already refused with invalid_argument_value by the explicit-start composition; a test now pins it. (5) Starting an item with an open blocker is out of scope and matches update semantics; filed as pm-urzubi.

value.text: CodeRabbit review round 2 on PR #1645: runMcpClaimAction now reads next only from the normalized runner options, so nested next:false overrides a flat next:true for both dispatch and the target check. The spec asserts {next:true, options:{next:false,start:true}} is refused with missing_required_argument instead of claiming an item.
